story.title: Pope Leo XIV Celebrates First Mass in Uruguay, Drawing Large Crowds
story.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated his first Mass in South America, attracting an estimated 40,000 attendees in Uruguay. During the event, he encouraged the crowd to foster fraternity and faith. A nighttime prayer vigil in Montevideo is anticipated to attract over 60,000 young participants.

explore_lenses.label: Why is a major papal event notable in Uruguay?
explore_lenses.title: A test of outreach in a secular society
explore_lenses.summary: The Mass is significant because Uruguay combines constitutional religious neutrality with comparatively low Catholic identification, making the visit an effort to engage believers and nonbelievers rather than a routine appearance in a strongly Catholic setting.

claims.text: Uruguay’s constitution protects religious freedom and says the state does not support any particular religion; the country also has an annual legal commemoration of secularism.
The most recent religious-affiliation figures cited by the U.S. State Department, from a 2014 Pew survey, found 42% of Uruguayans identified as Catholic and 37% as religiously unaffiliated.

Vatican communications coordinator Patricia Schroeder said organizers wanted the visit to reach the whole country, describing the pope as a potential messenger of peace and hope beyond Catholic audiences.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The affiliation data are dated, and a large one-day crowd does not establish whether religious practice or views will change.

explore_lenses.label: Why did the pope begin in Paysandú?
explore_lenses.title: A border-city Mass underscored regional ties
explore_lenses.summary: Paysandú offered a location accessible to pilgrims from neighboring countries and gave Leo a setting for his appeal to fraternity across borders.

claims.text: More than 30,000 people had registered in advance for the Mass, including pilgrims from Uruguay, Argentina and Brazil; the Vatican reported a further 10,000 attendees despite poor weather.
The Vatican’s published itinerary placed the Mass in Paysandú on November 7, between flights from and back to Montevideo, before other events in the capital.
In his homily, Leo used the nearby General Artigas international bridge and shared regional symbols to urge Catholics to become bridges and fraternal communities, especially for people in need.

explore_lenses.label: What comes next on the Uruguay stop?
explore_lenses.title: The visit shifts to youth and social concerns
explore_lenses.summary: After the Mass, Leo’s official program moves to Montevideo events focused on a violence-affected neighborhood, education and a youth prayer vigil, followed by a Sunday Mass in Florida before departure for Argentina.

claims.text: The Vatican program scheduled a meeting with Casavalle’s social community, an education-community event at the Catholic University of Uruguay and a prayer vigil at Centenary Stadium on November 7; it scheduled a Mass in Florida on November 8 before the flight to Buenos Aires.

Our Lady of Guadalupe parish in the Borro/Casavalle area supports housing, job creation and addiction recovery; AP reported that more than 46% of Montevideo’s 98 homicides through September occurred in Borro and nearby neighborhoods.
Forecast: organizers expected about 60,000 people at the Centenary Stadium vigil, according to Vatican News’ reporting before the event.

story_report.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated his first Mass in South America in Uruguay, drawing about 40,000 people and urging those present to build bridges of fraternity and faith. The gathering in Paysandú included pilgrims from Uruguay, Argentina and Brazil, according to advance registrations and Vatican reporting. The visit was set to continue with events in Montevideo, including a nighttime prayer vigil at Centenary Stadium that organizers expected to attract about 60,000 young people.

sections.heading: Uruguay’s Secular and Religious Setting
sections.body: The papal visit is taking place in a country whose constitution protects religious freedom and says the state supports no particular religion; Uruguay also has an annual legal commemoration of secularism. The most recent religious-affiliation figures cited by the U.S. State Department, drawn from a 2014 Pew survey, found that 42% of Uruguayans identified as Catholic while 37% were religiously unaffiliated. Vatican communications coordinator Patricia Schroeder said organizers hoped the visit would reach the whole country, portraying the pope as a messenger of peace and hope beyond Catholic audiences.

sections.heading: Montevideo Program Includes Casavalle Visit
sections.body: The Vatican program scheduled a meeting with Casavalle’s social community, an education-community event at the Catholic University of Uruguay and the Centenary Stadium vigil on November 7, followed by a Mass in Florida on November 8 before Leo’s flight to Buenos Aires. The Casavalle visit includes an area where Our Lady of Guadalupe parish supports housing, job creation and addiction recovery. AP reported that more than 46% of Montevideo’s 98 homicides through September occurred in Borro and nearby neighborhoods.

related_stories.title: Jay Rockefeller, Former Governor and Senator, Passes Away at 89
related_stories.summary: Jay Rockefeller, the last member of his family's political dynasty, has died at the age of 89. He served as the governor of West Virginia and was a longtime U.S. senator, known for his advocacy on healthcare, education, and working families' needs. Rockefeller was born into a prominent family and forged a significant political career.

related_stories.title: Momentum Builds for Coalition Talks in Israel as Eisenkot Gains Support
related_stories.summary: Following inconclusive elections, opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot is gaining momentum in his efforts to form a government in Israel. He has received significant backing, including from Arab parties, as President Isaac Herzog prepares to announce who will be tasked with forming the new government. Eisenkot aims to replace long-serving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
